paper_title: Hardness Results for Constant-Free Pattern Languages and Word Equations
classifications: Mathematics of computing → Combinatorics on words
statement: Is the equivalence problem of erasing pattern languages decidable?
context: The following questions remain open: Is the equivalence problem of erasing pattern languages decidable? Is the satisfiability problem of word equations in NP? For some fixed n ≥ 3, can we prove that EqSat(n, ?) is in P or NP or NP-hard?

paper_title: Hardness Results for Constant-Free Pattern Languages and Word Equations
classifications: Mathematics of computing → Combinatorics on words
statement: Is the satisfiability problem of word equations in NP?
context: Is the equivalence problem of erasing pattern languages decidable? Is the satisfiability problem of word equations in NP? For some fixed n ≥ 3, can we prove that EqSat(n, ?) is in P or NP or NP-hard? There are also several smaller open questions raised by the new results: Can the numbers 2560 and 2562 in Corollary 12 be made significantly smaller? This would require either a rather different approach or improving the results in [4]. Is EqSat(?, ?) polynomial-time reducible to EqSatCFNP (?, ?)? In Theorem 16, we used n + 2 new variables. Would a constant number of new variables be sufficient? The satisfiability problem remains NP-hard for several restricted subfamilies of word equations. Can we prove NP-hardness results for some interesting subfamilies of constantfree equations?
